key_insight: Helix4D adapts Trellis2's powerful frame-local attention to generate coherent dynamic 4D meshes from video by enabling selective cross-frame information sharing while preserving the pretrained model's ability to capture rare, challenging cases (transparent materials, thin structures, inner surfaces). This yields temporally consistent, topology-aware mesh sequences that handle complex scene changes.
problem_solved: Existing video-to-4D methods fail on complex topology changes, transparency, thin structures and inner surfaces; Helix4D addresses these by extending an expressive image-to-3D representation to video-conditioned dynamic mesh generation.
method: Inherit Trellis2's expressive frame-local attention representation and adapt it for temporal (4D) outputs.
Introduce mechanisms for selective cross-frame information sharing (temporal attention/communication) that preserve pretrained strengths on rare visual phenomena.
Produce dynamic mesh outputs via deformation-aware updates and topology-aware reconstruction to maintain temporal coherence across frames.
impact: Helix4D enables practitioners to recover high-fidelity, temporally consistent dynamic meshes from videos containing difficult materials and structural details, improving downstream tasks like animation, AR/VR content creation, and physical simulation with more robust geometry. It reduces failure cases in automated 4D reconstruction pipelines.
